question: Biopsy of a suspected juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA) in a teenage boy presenting with unilateral nasal obstruction and epistaxis should be avoided because the tumour is highly vascular and biopsy risks life-threatening haemorrhage.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Biopsy of JNA is contraindicated. The tumour is fed by the internal maxillary artery and is highly vascular; an inadvertent biopsy can cause torrential, potentially fatal haemorrhage. Always image first.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. JNA is the classic do-not-biopsy vascular nasal mass. Diagnosis is established by imaging (CT/MRI showing the Holman-Miller sign — anterior bowing of the posterior wall of the maxillary sinus). Pre-operative embolisation precedes surgical excision.
